text:
[gossipy, amused] Xavier So Based went from a park folding table to Barclays in four years.
On the Upper West Side, at twelve, he uploads his first beat.
In lockdown, his video game clan becomes a rap crew.
July twenty twenty-two: a laptop on a folding table, in a park, under fireworks.
That summer, Patch Made becomes a jerk anthem, now past two point five million views.
Then his stage dancing goes viral, and the scene can't stop arguing.
December twenty twenty-three: his show gets so packed, fans climb the fire escapes.
Somebody breaks the metal detector, and the show moves to a skate park.
By December twenty twenty-five, he sells out Webster Hall.
His album drops: Pitchfork says eight point three, Fantano says a strong five.
On a FADER shoot, he grabs go-kart thirty-four and is gone the whole race.
[whispers] But the tea? He told The FADER he never really listened to old jerk.
And in September, he opens for Ken Carson at Barclays.
Meanwhile his fans make their own hoodies, and the pile gets out of hand.
So one fan snaps the pile, and pile go lists it everywhere at once.
One hoodie sells, and it comes down everywhere else.
Folding table or Barclays: which era were you there for?
